title: Rule history (yg log read --aspect --json)
$comment: This schema describes exactly what this release of Yggdrasil writes: every mapping is closed and every enumeration lists only the values this release uses. Use it to check a producer. Do not use it to reject a document you read: under the family rule a later release may add a field or a value within /1, and a /1 reader ignores what it does not know (see family-contracts).

aspect.description: The rule whose history this is.

status.description: What the rule stands at right now — read from the rule, not from the log.

entries.description: Newest first. Capped only when the caller asked for a limit.

at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp — the entry header, verbatim.

body.description: Everything written under that header, verbatim.

status.description: Present only on an entry that recorded a change of standing.

ratified.description: Present only on an entry that recorded the user admitting the rule on the node types it reaches.

supersedes.description: Present when the entry replaces earlier entries of the rule's log: their datetimes.

supersededBy.description: Present when a later entry replaced this one: that entry's datetime.

types.description: The node types the admission covers.

version.description: The rule version admitted — a fingerprint of what the rule demanded then.

by.description: Who admitted it, as the entry names them.
